body:
Priority changed from `P4` to `P1` by the order of the maintainer, 2026-11-16. His words:

> "2235 focused on one thing to cache, i made another around caching in general.. we s hould raise that to P1, do it before 2246 and then isolate each cost and cache them"

Order of the work:

1. This issue first: step 1 (measure each frame cost, with a probe that stays in the suite) and step 2 (one cache rule, recorded).
2. Then each measured cost gets its own sub-issue and its own cache. #2246 (the filled area preview) is the first of them and waits for steps 1 and 2.

The work stacks on PR #2243 (the first cache and the first probe).

claimed: issue-worker-max (Opus) · 2026-11-16T19:31Z · worktree issue-2238 / issue/2238-frame-cost-rule · plan: steps 1-2 - measure each frame cost, record one cache rule, file a sub-issue for each cost

fix on issue/2238-frame-cost-rule · PR #2252 · pinned by frame_cost_probe::still_frames_on_fig8_name_their_costs · merges when reviewed (stacked on #2243)

Steps 1 and 2 are done: the probe and the rule (`docs/decisions/2238-frame-cost-rule.md`). Step 3 (move each cost to a cache) is in the sub-issues.

Work queue of the per-frame costs, by measured cost for each unchanged frame (release, fig8.step), largest first. The issue-2238 pair claims each issue. Each issue gets its own branch, stacked on `issue/2238-frame-cost-rule`.

| Queue | Issue | ms per frame | Cache key |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #2246 | 15.12 | the existing `Preview` key (`doc_version` + value hash of params, area, source); triangles made with the region |
| 2 | #2247 | 6.66 (4.68 + 1.98) | `Arc<Features>` allocation + picks value + view pose |
| 3 | #2248 | 4.24 (b), 1.22 (c) | picks value + params value + setup + `Arc<Features>` of each picked entity and the stock + transforms + units |
| 4 | #2249 | 4.13 | the selection-walk memo of #2248 (same key) |
| 5 | #2250 | 1.48 | picks value + `Arc<Features>` + view pose + hidden set |

Explorer reading, not measured yet: #2248 and #2249 run the same selection walk, and `region_of` for `Side::Auto` runs it a third time. One memo can serve all three.

Stack table for the frame-cost queue. Release build, fig8, `frame_cost_probe::still`, ms for each still frame. The "after" column is measured on the head of the last PR (fd68dfd90), so it includes all the PRs below.

| PR | Issue | Branch | Head |
|---|---|---|---|

| #2255 | #2246 | `issue/2246-area-preview-fill` | f6c7f605f |

Each PR is stacked on the PR above it. Retarget each child to `main` before its parent merges.

| State | Before | After #2255 | After #2266 |
|---|---|---|---|
| a nothing selected | 3.5 | - | 3.8 |
| b contour, top chains | 13.1 | 14.1 | 5.1 |
| c 2D Adaptive, welded face, preview | 30.0 | 14.8 | 6.0 |
| d toolpath shown | 3.3 | - | 3.6 |
| e simulation paused | 3.4 | - | 4.1 |

The a, d and e values are in the run-to-run noise. On each still frame of states a-e, the probe counts zero region builds, chain walks, digests, slices, patch groupings, selection walks and pick line builds.

Pieces that stay over 0.5 ms on a still frame:

- `ui/viewport.pick_ink` in state c: 0.91 ms.
- `scene/collect` in total: about 1.2-1.7 ms (models, grid, toolpaths).
- `ui/viewport`, `ui/browser`, `ui/status`: 0.4-0.7 ms each.

`operation::region_of` still walks the selection on a changed input. It does not walk on a still frame.

Test build (not launched): `.claude/tmp/test-builds/camcraft-framecost-fd68dfd90.exe`.

Measurement of the frame target, no code change.

- Commit: d3e779907 (origin/main).
- Mode: release (`cargo test -p camcraft-ui --release --lib -j 6 still_frames_on_fig8 -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`).
- Probe: `egui_app::tests::frame_cost_probe::still_frames_on_fig8_name_their_costs`. There is no `frame_cost_ops_probe` on main.
- Scene: `testdata/models/fig8.step`, still frames, 6 frames for each state. Each value is the median of 3 runs.

Frame total in ms (commands + scene + ui):

| State | Commands | Scene | UI | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a nothing selected | 0.00 | 1.46 | 2.08 | 3.5 |
| b chains selected | 0.01 | 1.52 | 3.02 | 4.6 |
| c 2D Adaptive area preview | 0.01 | 1.59 | 4.24 | 5.8 |
| d toolpath shown | 0.00 | 1.17 | 2.23 | 3.4 |
| e simulation paused | 0.00 | 1.17 | 2.26 | 3.4 |

Named costs above 1 ms (median of 3 runs, ms per frame):

| Cost | a | b | c | d | e | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scene/collect` | 1.41 | 1.48 | 1.53 | 1.13 | 1.13 | `world::collect`, timed in the probe |
| `ui/viewport` | 0.97 | 1.13 | 2.26 | 0.64 | 0.66 | `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs:247` |
| `ui/viewport.pick_ink` | 0.01 | 0.17 | 1.31 | - | - | `shell.rs:624` (`pick_ink::paint`) |

Other costs are below 1 ms. The largest are `ui/properties` (0.72-0.89 in b and c), `ui/viewport.labels` (0.64, `shell.rs:602`) and `ui/browser` (0.50-0.57, `shell.rs:259`). On each still frame the probe counts zero region builds, walks, digests, slices, patch groupings, selection walks and pick line builds. The pick_ink value varies from 0.95 to 1.51 between runs.

Result: under 10 ms. The worst state (c) is 5.8 ms.

The probe does not cover:
- hover, mouse move, orbit, pan, zoom or any frame that changes input;
- a live GPU frame (the probe runs the egui test harness, with no wgpu draw or present);
- the first frame after an input change;
- scenes other than fig8, or a larger model.

The maintainer decided on 2026-11-17: "Measure, then close or split". The measurement is in the comment above.

Result on main at `d3e779907` (release build, `frame_cost_probe::still_frames_on_fig8_name_their_costs`, median of three runs): each still frame of the fig8 scene is under 10 ms. The largest is 5.8 ms (2D Adaptive area preview). The caches that give this result merged with the PRs of #2201, #2209 and #2235.

This issue is closed on that reading. The probe does not measure these cases:

- hover, orbit, pan and zoom frames, and the first frame after a change;
- a live GPU frame;
- scenes with many operations.

Issue #2201 stays open for the cost with many operations and for a probe with hover and orbit (its cost rows 1 to 9). Reopen this issue if a measured frame is above 10 ms.
